page.layout: Running head at top, centred; page number at top right. Two woodcut medallions (coin portraits) side by side above the text, not text blocks. One column of running text below them, with a paragraph beginning at the top and a second paragraph lower down. Signature at the foot right.

main_text.p: PYRRHVS, patre Epirotarum Rege in exilium acto, furtim subtractus ad Illyricos bimus defertur, vbi Rex eum ad-optat, protegitque aduersus Cassandrum Macedoniæ Regem. his rebus moti Epirotæ, odio in misericordiam verso, eum in regnum reuocant. Adolescens multa bella gesit, tantóq; suc-cessu, ut Tarentinos solus aduersus Romanos tueri posse videretur. Romanos elephantis primum visis territos, vincit, vulne-ratus ipse: ducentos captiuos milites gratis Romam remittit. Syracusas veniens, multas ciuitates dum subigit, Rex Siciliæ sicut Epiri appellatur: filiis, Heleno, Siciliæ, Alexandro, Italiæ regnum destinat: postea bella aliquot feliciter cum Carthagi-nensibus gerit. tandem ex Sicilia abiens, dixisse fertur, O qualem Carthaginensibus & Romanis pro hac insula palæstram relinquimus! A Pœnis nauali prælio victus, ab Antigono, de quo supra, au-xiliares milites petit: non obtinës, repente Antigonum vincit, fugat, Macedoniam capit, anno mundi 3 6 7 6. ante Christum natû 286. Iam Græciæ, Asiæque regna meditatur: nec illi maior ex imperio quam ex bello voluptas: à Spartanis tamen, maxi-mè a mulieribus, non fortius quàm verecundius victus, rece-dit: Ptolemæum filium amittit. Pulsus à Spartanis Argos petit, vbi Antigonum oppugnans, atque inter confertissimos hostes fortissimè dimicans, saxo de muris iactato, occiditur. Vide Iu-stin. lib. 17. 18. 23. 25. Plutar. in Pyr. & Oro. lib. 4. cap. 1. 2. 3.
ALEXANDER, Pyrrhi filius, ulcisci patris mortem cupiens, Macedoniæ fines populatur: Antigonus transsitione militum destitutus, regnum cum exercitu amittit. Iusti. lib. 26.

page.notes: Two woodcut coin portraits above the text, with legends around the rims: left "PYRRHVS·REX·EPIR", right "ALEXANDER·REX·EPIR·" (the second legend partly curved and hard to read). Long s rendered as s throughout. "Caffandrum" and "transfitione" printed with long s and ff/fi forms, transcribed as Cassandrum and transsitione. "Carthagi-nensibus", "vulne-ratus", "ad-optat", "au-xiliares", "rece-dit", "suc-cessu" and "Iu-stin" keep their printed hyphens at line ends. Numbers "3 6 7 6." and "286" copied as printed.
